options.lead: Every beam of light in this hall is a program drawing its own path.
lines: Click a laser, a lens or a beam. Press Program.
Change a number, predict, then press Save.
options.footnote: The light is slowed down about a hundred million times so you can watch it.

params.text: All the light is cleared. Press any green arrow to draw it again.

options.title: A ray is a model
options.body: Real light is a wave. Here each beam follows three rules: go straight, bounce off mirrors, bend at glass and water. A beam cannot see the glass. Its program is told where the glass is, in the green blocks at the top.

options.title: Ibn Sahl and Ibn al-Haytham
options.body: The law of refraction was first written down by Ibn Sahl in Baghdad in 984, six centuries before Snell. Ibn al-Haytham's Book of Optics, written in Cairo soon after 1011, began testing ideas about light by experiment.

options.title: THE MIRROR
options.caption: Angle in = angle out. The marks show the starting angle.
info: Click the red bead. Press Program.
Change angle from -25 to -20, then -30.
Predict where the dot lands first.
Try -35 too. What happens?

params.text: Over the top of the screen. Try a smaller angle.

options.title: The mirror rule is one block
options.caption: The beam turns its own angle upside down at the mirror.

options.title: THE PERISCOPE
options.caption: Two mirrors at 45 degrees let a low eye see over a wall.
info: A mirror at angle m: out = 2m - in.
At -45°, flat turns straight down, and back.
The right-hand periscope is empty.

params.text: The eye sees the laser from behind the wall.

options.title: Program the empty periscope
options.target: Click the yellow bead (no green arrow), press Program:
options.tip: Each mirror turns the light a quarter turn. Press Save and watch the eye.

options.title: THE WATER TANK
options.caption: Snell's law: n1 sin i = n2 sin r, measured from the normal.
info: Light slows down in water and bends.
Click the red bead. Set n to 1: no bend.
Set n to 2.417: a tank of diamond.
Grey: where the fish seems to be.

params.text: A spear thrown where the fish seems to be goes past it.

options.title: Snell's law in five blocks

steps.text: set si to sin° of i
set r to asin° of t

options.caption: i and r are measured from the normal. Air is n = 1.

options.title: THE LIGHT PIPE
options.caption: Left: when the maths has no answer. Right: a fibre.
info: Glass to air: sin r = 1.52 × sin i.
Past 41.1°, that is more than 1,
and no angle has a sine above 1.
So the light cannot get out. It reflects.

marks.text: every bounce is total internal reflection

params.text: Light escaped at a wall. Try a smaller angle.
{bounces} bounces, and none of the light got out.

options.title: When the maths has no answer
options.target: Click the red bead in the glass. Set i to 45, press Save. Then fix it:

steps.text: set r to asin° of t

options.tip: Drag the two blocks under "set t" into the first if. Then try i = 30, 40, 45, 60.

options.title: THE PRISM
options.caption: Dense flint glass. White light comes apart.
info: Every colour has its own n.
Click any colour bead and read it:
n is the only number that differs.
Newton did this with sunlight in 1666.

params.text: Violet bends the most. Red bends the least.

options.title: THE LENS
options.caption: Every ray parallel to the axis meets at the focus.
info: tan(new angle) = tan(angle) - h ÷ f
h: how high the ray crosses the lens.
Click the lens. Change f from 6 to 4, then 9.
Your eye focuses by changing its own f.

params.text: The beams meet {f} feet past the lens.
